name: 3-Isocyanatopropyltriethoxysilane
description: 3-Isocyanatopropyltriethoxysilane (CAS 24801-88-5 ), also known as ICPTES, is a bifunctional silane coupling agent combining an isocyanate group with an alkoxysilane anchor. It bonds organic polymer matrices to inorganic substrates by reacting at both the organic and inorganic interface simultaneously. This versatile chemical is used for glass, metals, and mineral fillers. In adhesives, sealants, and structural bonding formulations, it improves adhesion to glass and metal substrates where moisture resistance is critical for long-term performance. Coatings manufacturers use it to crosslink polyurethane systems onto treated surfaces, improving durability and intercoat adhesion on automotive and industrial parts. It ensures a robust chemical bond between the coating and the underlying material. In filled polymer compounds, it functions as a surface modifier for silica and glass fiber, improving stress transfer between filler and matrix in reinforced plastics. This leads to enhanced mechanical properties and structural integrity. Electronics encapsulants and underfill resins incorporate it to enhance interfacial adhesion between polymer and substrate under thermal cycling conditions. This prevents delamination and protects sensitive electronic components from environmental stress. Supplied as a clear to pale yellow liquid in standard packaging from small laboratory quantities up to bulk drums and IBC containers. Technical grade is the primary commercial offering, with purity typically at 95% or higher. Moisture-sensitive handling requirements influence packaging specifications, and nitrogen-blanketed containers are standard for bulk shipments.
